one_line_contribution: A variance-components audit of per-item counterfactual credit in an LLM agent's experience bank: split leave-one-out item credit into a between-item SD and re-run noise, show that within a class of same-type expert items the between-item SD is indistinguishable from zero, and price in re-runs what a reliable per-item rank, a top-quartile selection, and a pruning decision actually cost.
closest_prior_work: Data Banzhaf (arxiv:2205.15466, verified via s2cli: AISTATS, 196 citations) is the real threat and the proposal cites it correctly. It already establishes the paper's motivating fact — under a stochastic value function, LOO and Shapley data values are rank-unstable and the observed spread is substantially estimator noise — and proposes the noise-robust semivalue as the fix. What it does not do is separate a between-item variance component from a re-run variance component, report a reliability-versus-sample-count curve, or work on retrieved in-context experience consumed by a multi-step agent; its substrate is retraining on supervised data. SCARV (arxiv:2605.00944, verified) covers stable sample ranking under redundancy, again on static datasets. So the transposition is defensible, but the intellectual core — 'the ranking you are scoring is mostly noise, and here is the sample cost of an honest one' — is Banzhaf's finding plus classical test theory (Spearman-Brown, disattenuation, generalizability theory), applied to a new substrate. On the agent side I verified AttriMem 2607.21106, MemQ 2605.08374, RoMeRL 2608.02508, HiMPO 2606.16285, SF-AMS 2607.22562, TreeMem 2605.04811 (actual title 'Tree-based Credit Assignment for Multi-Agent Memory System') and 2507.04480 (actual title 'Source Attribution in Retrieval-Augmented Generation', PKDD/ECML workshop, not 'Shapley-RAG'); none reports a between-item variance component or a re-run budget, so the gap claim survives. I also verified Data Shapley 1904.02868, FreeShap 2406.04606, amortized Shapley 2305.19998, OddSHAP 2602.01399, and Memory-R2 2605.21768 (2026-05-20, credit assignment for memory-augmented agents, RL-side, not an attribution-variance study). I did not verify 2605.05583, 2602.00428, 2607.06503, 2601.20090, 2110.01307 or 2107.11357 from the proposal's collision check; none is load-bearing for its novelty argument.
strongest_objection: The headline null is close to being manufactured by the composition it is scored in, and the proposal supplies the arithmetic itself. In C1 the HOLE set still contains two correct same-type expert exemplars, so by the authors' own k-sweep any single item's marginal is bounded near k3 - k2 ~ 4 net; a between-item SD of 8 net among items whose true means are all compressed into a ~4-net band is essentially unreachable unless some expert items are actively harmful, which the design neither plants nor controls. So P1's falsifier is not reachable by the mechanism the falsifier names, and 'tau_E < 5 net' measures a ceiling the design imposed rather than a property of expert experience items. The offered estimator gate does not repair this: the pooled E+W class has a spread planted between classes by P3's 15-net separation, so passing it certifies only that the estimator recovers a between-class difference, never that C1 can express a within-E difference at all. A reviewer will read the headline as 'we compressed the range and then reported that the range is small'. The secondary objection is that the prediction set is one estimate wearing five hats: R(m) = tau^2/(tau^2 + sigma^2/m) is a plug-in identity in tau_S and sigma measured on the very same pairs (P4), winner's-curse retention ~ R(m) is the textbook regression-to-the-mean identity applied to those same 200 halvings (P5), and the pruning-precision curve is a deterministic function of P3's W-E separation and sigma (P6). P4-P6 are calibration checks of an additive-normal model, not independent tests, and the proposal concedes they share one cell; a skeptical AC will count two genuinely open predictions (P2, P3) out of seven.
what_would_fix_it: Promote C2 (the item as the sole same-type procedure carrier) to the primary composition for P1 rather than the fallback, so that the estimand is not capped at ~4 net before measurement, and re-budget accordingly — C2 currently gets 16 E items at 8 games x 2 seeds, far too thin to carry the headline. Second, add a within-class positive control that C1 and C2 must both pass before any null is scored: expert items planted with a graded quality gradient inside E (truncated procedures, a correct-but-off-object exemplar, verbose-but-correct, partially-correct recovery traces), so a known non-zero within-class tau has to be recovered; the E+W gate cannot substitute for this, because it is a between-class contrast. Third, add an identical-item duplicate pair (the same item entered under two ids) to give an empirical zero-spread reference for the estimator. Fourth, restate P4 and P6 as residuals against the plug-in curve recomputed from the measured tau and sigma with a pre-registered discrepancy bound, so they carry information the components do not already contain, and keep the seed-split versus game-split clause as the one genuinely separate test. Finally, either drop P7(c) or raise backbone 2 to >= 32 paired re-runs per item and state its falsifier explicitly against the attenuation ceiling sqrt(R1 R2) rather than an absolute 0.3, since at 16 paired re-runs the tau_S CI upper bound essentially cannot fall below the stated falsifying threshold.
missing_baseline: A within-class positive control for the headline cell: expert items planted with a known quality gradient inside E (and/or the same item duplicated under two ids as an empirical zero-spread reference), measured in C1 itself. Every other control in the plan is between-class (E vs W) or between-arm (k3 vs k0, static3), so nothing in the design demonstrates that the C1 estimator can recover a within-class between-item SD when one exists — which is exactly the quantity P1 reports as null. A reviewer will also ask for the naive decision baseline the pruning claim is really competing against: rank items by the free nested-k position credit already in the k-sweep logs, or simply by natural retrieval rank and item length, and show that paired re-runs beat it at equal cost; the proposal places the proxy and slot credit on the reliability-cost curve but never lets a zero-re-run heuristic compete on P6's precision task.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. Queries I ran, all through the s2cli channel (S2+HF, both ok; WebSearch unavailable in this session, WebFetch never used): (1) 'between-item variance decomposition of leave-one-out counterfactual credit for retrieved memory items in LLM agents' --recent -> 10 hits, the closest being AttriMem 2607.21106, MemQ 2605.08374, Memory-R2 2605.21768, A-MAC 2603.04549 and counterfactual credit for multi-agent collaboration 2603.21563; all assign credit, none measures whether item-level credit exceeds its own measurement noise. (2) 'variance components split-half reliability of instance-level data value estimates, how many repeated runs for a stable ranking' -> On Randomness in Agentic Evals 2602.07150, Beyond pass@1 reliability science 2603.29231, Quantifying Variance in Evaluation Benchmarks 2406.10229, ReasonBENCH 2512.07795 — arm-level and benchmark-level run variance, not item-level value variance. (3) 'Data Banzhaf noise-robust data valuation ranking stability' -> returned 2205.15466 directly this time, plus generic robustness work; verified. (4) 'generalizability theory variance components reliability of item-level effect estimates, psychometrics for model evaluation' --recent -> IRT reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge 2602.00521, ATLAS 2511.04689, Fluid Benchmarking 2509.11106 — the nearest home literature, none about counterfactual item credit. (5) in-context demonstration valuation with LOO removal and seed instability --recent -> 'When Correct Demonstrations Hurt' 2605.26350 and a paired-bootstrap evaluation protocol 2511.19794; neither makes the claim. (6) winner's-curse / selection on noisy estimates -> nothing relevant. (7) 'episodes needed to estimate per-item memory utility, pruning precision' --recent -> nothing relevant. Judging the proposal's own check: it is above the round's average — five queries, each with its channel named, IDs given, and one honest negative (its Banzhaf query failed to return Banzhaf, which it says, then verifies the id directly). Two gaps count against it: it never searched its actual mechanism's home vocabulary (reliability, variance components, split-half, generalizability theory) despite the whole analysis being classical test theory, and it never searched in-context-demonstration valuation, the obvious adjacent framing for 'retrieved exemplar consumed in a prompt'. I ran both and found no pre-emption, so the novelty claim stands on my searches, not on the proposal's.
